newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTUGAL FEDERATION SUES TV OVER DRUGS ROW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTUGAL FEDERATION SUES TV OVER DRUGS ROW.

text.p: The Portuguese Soccer Federation said on Tuesday it would sue the country's leading private television station over allegations Portuguese players smoked hashish before an international.
Denouncing the allegations as "false", the federation said it was taking action against "the SIC television station for damage caused to the image of the country's football."

It said it was also opening "criminal proceedings" against those who had taken part in the programme in which a Brazilian prostitute claimed to have attended a party at the players' hotel where hashish was smoked.
The incidents were said to have occurred before a European championship game against Ireland in November 1995.

The allegations, the latest in a series of scandals rocking the game, had already triggered a writ from Portuguese champions Porto, some of whose players were said by SIC to have been involved in the incidents.
The federation said the allegations had been investigated and shown to be false after they had first surfaced in a newspaper article in December 1995.
"We can deny the version presented in that (television) programme," the federation said in its statement.

In the programme, a Brazilian prostitute identified only as 'Paula' said she had gone to the players' hotel with a group of friends but the party had ended in violence and she had needed treatment at a nearby hospital.
The television station quoted an anonymous member of a private security firm in support of its charges.
But the federation said neither the hotel's management nor the security firm had reported anything unusual happening the night on which the incidents were supposed to have occurred.
Players named in the programme have denied the incidents and the Portuguese players' union has said it would also be pressing for an investigation into the affair.
Portugal won the match 3-0 and went on to qualify for the championships in England where they reached the quarter-finals.

Portuguese soccer has been hit by a series of scandals in recent months, ranging from allegations of attempts to bribe referees to an incident in which former international striker, Ricardo Sa Pinto of Sporting, knocked national coach Artur Jorge to the ground after being excluded from the national team.
The Federation announced on Tuesday that it had banned Sa Pinto from the national squad until after the 1998 World Cup finals in France.
